title: Reranker failover profiles and geofenced fanout for low-latency, high-availability scoring
creator: Avery Chen
description: Implement a multi-pronged resilience approach for the reranking endpoint to improve tail latency, reduce customer-visible errors, and enable predictable scaling: 1) adaptive timeout profiles per workload, 2) multi-tier circuit breakers (node/pool/region), 3) geofenced fanout + preferred-region routing with cost-aware fallbacks, 4) warm pool and pre-warming hooks for heavy queries, and 5) KV-prefix caching alignment between embeddings and reranker to reduce cold compute. This ticket covers design, implementation, rollout plan, and observability requirements.
tasks: Design adaptive timeout profiles and SLO mapping (p50/p95/p99) for small/medium/large requests
Add multi-tier CB implementation: local (per-node) -> pool -> region; expose metrics and config via Console
Implement preferred-region routing with geofence table and cost thresholds; add automatic downgrade to a compatible model variant when preferred region exhausted
Build warm-pool orchestration for long-context models and heavy rerank requests; integrate with autoscale signals
Coordinate embedding cache alignment: prefix-based KV reuse and cache warming strategy before rerank invocation
Create canary rollout with traffic shaping and progressive ramp for Dedicated and Hosted tenants
Add observability dashboards: per-tenant SLO heatmap, CB trips, fallback counts, tail latency breakdowns
E2E tests including chaos injection (network/latency) and synthetic large payloads
Document API/SDK behavior changes and updated error codes for fallbacks
acceptance_criteria: Tail P99 latency for rerank endpoint reduced by >= 25% on representative workload (internal benchmark)
Fallbacks (regional/model downgrade) trigger on CB trip and successfully return compatible results with <1% regression in relevance on evaluation prompts
Circuit breaker state exposed in Console and supports operator override for emergency bypass
No customer errors increase > 0.5% during canary for Hosted customers; Dedicated tenants tested in staging cluster
End-to-end test suite with chaos scenarios passes in CI and included in nightly regression
monitoring: Metric: rerank.request.latency.{p50,p95,p99} by region, model, tenant
Log: per-request routing decisions (sampled) with reason codes
Synthetic canary probe: hourly relevance and latency probes per-region
rollout_plan: Phase 0: deploy canary to internal cluster; run synthetic load and chaos for 48h
Phase 1: enable for 5% of small-scale Hosted traffic with feature flag; monitor SLOs for 72h
Phase 2: enable preferred-region routing for Dedicated staging customers and run integration tests with their config
Phase 3: progressive ramp to 50% then 100% for Hosted after 7 days of stability
Phase 4: documentation and SDK release with explicit deprecation notes for any removed behaviors
testing_plan: Unit tests for circuit breaker state transitions and metrics emissions
Integration tests for routing decisions with mocked region capacity responses
Load tests: realistic token distributions with embedding + rerank pipeline at 1x and 3x expected load
Chaos tests: simulate inter-region network partition and high tail P99 latency nodes
Relevance regression: evaluate 10k representative prompts to ensure fallback quality meets threshold
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Incorrect fallback could return semantically incompatible results -> run A/B quality checks and conservative fallback gating
Risk: CB misconfiguration could over-trip causing availability loss -> expose operator override and safe cooldown windows
Risk: Warm pools increase cost if mis-sized -> implement sizing heuristics based on recent QPS and use burstable instances
Risk: Per-tenant SLO heterogeneity complicates routing -> support tenant-level profile overrides and default conservative profile
implementation_notes: Prefer non-blocking state machine in runtime for CB to avoid global locks
Use existing routing layer hooks; add routing decision reason codes for traceability
Leverage existing autoscaler signals (queue_depth, cpu_util, kv_cache_hit_rate) to trigger warm-pool pre-warming
Add small migration shim to preserve legacy error codes for one release cycle
Coordinate with Console team to add circuit-breaker controls and SLO visualization (Console backlog ticket already queued)
